Minister of Police Nkandla Report

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Nkandla saga continues- Minister of Police eleases his report

Summary:
Public Protector Thuli Madonsela tasked the Minster of Police and the Minister of Finance to detail the costs of the non security upgrades of Presidents Zuma's Nkandla homestead. Instead the Minister of Police delivered a 50 page report on Thursday which concluded that all four items identified as personal upgrades were if fact essential security features and therefore should be paid with State funds as President Zuma.
The President kicked off his Budget Speech by taunting the Opposition mocking newly elected DA Leader MMusi Maimane and the EFF, his ebullient attitude on the eve of the release of the report indicated he was happy with the findings of the Police Ministers report

Opposition parties are outraged although not that surprised as the Minister of Police is appointed by President Zuma and forms part of his Cabinet. The Nkandla debate started in 2011 and doesn't seem to be going away soon.

Press Release:


Nkandla Report
A year ago Public Protector Thuli Madonsela published her Nkandla report, stating Zuma and his family had personally benefited from millions spent on improving his private home. In Parliament this week President Jacob Zuma mocked opposition MPs who had persistently raised questions about Nkandla. A day later, Police Minister Nathi Nhleko’s long-awaited report found the President was not liable for the cost of security upgrades to his home. Carte Blanche reports on the contentious findings.


Script:


Link: Jacob Zuma was back in Parliament this week and unsurprisingly the Nkandla controversy returned to the spotlight, only this time the President was on the offensive which what he said was their preoccupation with the issue. His mood apparently buoyed by what his police Minister would announce 24 hours later.
Zuma “Nkandla even if you are discussing very serious matters, and they stand up, point of order, yes Nkandla tito …. Heeee
Script: Newly elected leader of the DA Mmusi Maimane took the brunt of the Presidents taunts
Zuma “A broken man, a broken country, ….
Mmusi “I almost feel it’s a man who is in complete disdain of the people of South Africa, someone who stands up and says ‘I can do as I please and you’ll do nothing. There’s also a level at which you cry for the beloved country
Script: The EFF Deputy Secretary General Hlengiwe Hlope was equally incensed by the President
Hlophe “He thought that he was making joke against us as EFF as opposition party but the world even the Sa were very disappointed on him
Zuma “ Some people who could not pronounce Nkandla, they have now learned Nkandla Nkandla Nkandla Heeeee
Script: Gaye Davis EWN chief parliamentary reporter has been watching the Nkandla saga closely since it first erupted in 2011
Gaye Davis “ One thing for sure though we know why the president was just so ebullient in the house during his debate on his budget vote he had seen the report and clearly liked what he had seen.
Script: The Police Ministers report was supposed to investigate what the Public Protectors “Secure in Comfort” report had exposed. She found that the president and his family had unduly befitted from the upgrade which could not be justified in the name of security. There was the 2,8 million Rand for a swimming pool which we were told would double as a firepool, because of the unreliable water supply in the area.
Thuli “ A swimming pool that is used as a fire-pool how about an ordinary water reservoir it’s much it’s cheaper.”
Script” The other features were a cattle kraal, a chicken run, a visitor’s centre, an amphitheatre, and extensive paving, 8 million rand was also spent to relocate Zumas neighbours. She stated in her report that this was unconscionable, excessive, and a misappropriation of public funds.
Link: But in the Police Minister report 50 page report he contradicted those interpretations saying all four are vital to the homesteads security.
Script: After reading the full 50 page report the Minister concluded
Min “Accordingly the State President is not liable to pay for any of the security features”
Script” At a Press conference immediately after the briefing the DA expressed its outrage at what they described as a whitewash
Mmuzi “Min Nathi Nhlekos determination that President Zuma is not liable for any of the lavish upgrades is in fact obscene and an insult to the South African people.
Hlengiwe Hllope “ We feel that this is an insult to the nation, although we are not totally shocked because we know, the Minister is an deployee, he is employed by Zuma
Link: Minister Nhlekos report as completed on the 25 March this year but was only handed to parliament two months later that’s left opposition parties asking, why the delay
Mmusi “This is a cynical manipulation of due process by not affording Parliament the opportunity to interrogate the report. The President is sending a clear message that corruption does not matter and that he is above the law”
Mhlengeni “I think they took a political decisions as Cabinet Ministers to say just let us protect him, to protect him it means we will be protected as well as the Ministers here.
Gaye “There was a plan not to release the report ahead of the Presidency budget vote because the opposition MPs would have had a field day instead it was the President that was able to have the upper hand
Script: Head of political studies at Wits University Daryl Glazer says that despite what the opposition says, President Zuma remains secure
“He has demonstrated an amazing survival ability and an amazing willingness to brazen things out so I would say that right now his position looks strong and I would say the only thing that could upset his position would be an unexpectedly bad performance in next year’s local elections“
Script: The Police Ministers report is the 7th commissioned on the Nkandla saga to date. This one stood out for its inclusion of four videos illustrating the Police Ministers findings, complete with a dramatic sound track
It was also the first footage shot inside the President homestead.
The local fire Manager Mr Xulu went to great lengths showing the value of the firepool and the failure of the fire hydrants installed on the property
Upsound ”A Firepool is an excellent source of water”
Script: But the nature of the Police Minister investigation left DA chief whip John Steenhuisen cold
“This report is sloppy it is badly put together, the research methodology is something that a matic student would use using Wikipedia and Google to deal with some very serious facts”
Link ”The Police Minster report includes the claim that the various investigations undertaken around Nkandla have themselves constituted a security risk
Min Mhleko “The extent of the investigation as well as the intrusion into the private residence of the President has resulted in a violation of his rights”
Link. “It is for that reason it says that the unfinished security upgrades need to be competed and possibly new ones undertaken but the Department of Public Works says that he has no idea how much that process is going to cost.
Script” The Public Protector wasn’t given prior access to the report and only spoke out in interview on 702 on Friday evening. She said the Minister had failed to do his job as he was supposed to determine where the 52.9 Million rand was spent, the probe was supposed to be undertaken with the Minister of Finance
Thuli “He was only asked to determine the amount, he was never asked to make comments on my report so I don’t know what the basis of that report that was issued. Is it a new investigation? Is it a review because it doesn’t review any report it just makes comments. I never asked him to do anything like that”
Minister” The Public Protectors recommendation is very clear there is in proper benefit arising out of measures of security to derive non security comfort
Script “ The Minister went on to say that Madonsela incorrectly categorised certain non- security upgrades. His report has determined that they are in fact crucial to Nkandla security.
John “So what now for Thuli Modonsela’s report?”
Gaye “ as far as I can see the Public Protector report is in a kind of limbo , there are many questions that she put to President Zuma about the spending and about his knowledge of the spending and many of them were not answered.”
Daryl “ I think Nkandla is going to dog the president until the end of the term of his office it is quite clear that the opposition party are unified behind a commitment of keeping this issue alive … it is certainly going to continue to shadow his presidency whether it’s going to do him damage that is more doubtful.
Link” The police Minister report will now be sent to the parliamentary ad hoc committee for further interrogation but the opposition is concerned that the ANC’s track record on the issue the document will merely be given a rubber stamp and it is for that reason that the Democratic Alliance is considering going to court
Musi “We are fighting this case at every level, there are key matters that require thorough testing here, so that the president knows the Public Protector is not simply an ombudsman but that in fact the remedial actions are enforceable
John “Are we going to see you and the rest of your colleagues still standing up shouting pay back the money?
Hlengiwe” We are still going to say this matter must not rest, this matter must come back until this man who benefited unduly he must pay back the money
Script: The Nkandla debate has been raging in parliament since 2011 and, judging by the fallout from this latest report, it’s an issue unlikely to go away any time soon.
